questions.question: Which discretionary power allows a Governor to reserve a bill passed by the state legislature for the consideration of the President?
questions.option_1: To send a report to the President for the imposition of President's Rule.
questions.option_2: To reserve a bill for the President's consideration.
questions.option_3: To grant pardon in certain cases.
questions.option_4: To summon, prorogue, and dissolve the state legislative assembly.
questions.solution: Under Article 200, the Governor has the power to assent to a bill, withhold assent, return the bill, or reserve the bill for the President's consideration, especially if it endangers the position of the State High Court.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) is most accurate?
questions.option_1: UCC is enforceable only when ratified by all religious communities through a national referendum.
questions.option_2: The Law Commission of India (2018) recommended UCC for all religions to ensure uniformity.
questions.option_3: The Supreme Court has uniformly declared UCC as mandatory across states.
questions.option_4: The UCC is already implemented in Goa and Uttarakhand through their respective legislative frameworks.
questions.solution: Goa has followed a Common Civil Code (Portuguese era) since its liberation. In 2024, Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to pass and implement its own Uniform Civil Code (UCC) legislation.

questions.question: As per the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which of the following best defines "electronic communication"?
questions.option_1: Any information transmitted using electronic devices like phones or computers
questions.option_2: Only video calls conducted through secure government networks
questions.option_4: Verbal messages sent through written documents only
questions.solution: In BNSS, 2023, 'electronic communication' is defined broadly as the transmission of any written, verbal, pictorial info, or video content using electronic devices like telephones, computers, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following best reflects the constitutional dilemma in implementing the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in India?
questions.option_1: UCC allows gender-based personal law systems to remain untouched under Article 14
questions.option_2: UCC enforces cooperative federalism by giving states legislative powers on personal law
questions.option_3: UCC operationalises the secular ethos by completely eliminating all religious laws
questions.option_4: UCC aligns with Article 44 but may be seen to infringe upon religious freedom under Article 25
questions.solution: The dilemma exists between Article 44 (Directive Principle for UCC) and Article 25 (Fundamental Right to practice religion). While UCC aims for a common law, some argue it interferes with religious practices protected as fundamental rights.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements holds true regarding the Governor's executive powers?
1. Governor is state's constitutional head.
2. He acts solely on Council's advice.
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct (Article 153/154). Statement 2 is incorrect because while the Governor generally acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers (Article 163), he also has discretionary powers where he can act independently.

questions.question: Under Section 25(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, what may the Court do when a person is convicted in one trial for multiple offences?
questions.option_1: Can impose only one punishment for all the offences, regardless of their nature
questions.option_2: Must give the harshest punishment only and remit other punishments altogether
questions.option_3: Shall suspend all sentences unless directed by a higher court in the same trial
questions.option_4: May impose punishments to run either concurrently or consecutively as appropriate
questions.solution: Under Section 25 of BNSS, the court has the discretion to decide if multiple sentences should run concurrently (all at once) or consecutively (one after the other).

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of newly created States and their year of creation is correctly matched?
questions.solution: In 2000, three states were created: Chhattisgarh (Nov 1), Uttarakhand (Nov 9), and Jharkhand (Nov 15). Telangana was created much later in 2014.

questions.question: Which Indian state does S. Jaishankar represent in the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution: The External Affairs Minister, S. Jaishankar, was elected to the Rajya Sabha from the state of Gujarat.

questions.question: The National Population Register (NPR) was created under the provisions of which Act and Rules?
questions.solution: The National Population Register (NPR) is prepared under the provisions of the Citizenship Act, 1955 and the Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003.

questions.question: The concept of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) originated in which country?
questions.solution: The concept of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) originated in the United States of America (USA) in the 1960s. In India, it was pioneered by Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer.

questions.question: Which state has no Panchayati Raj Institution at all?
questions.solution: Under the 73rd Amendment, certain areas are exempted. The Panchayati Raj system does not exist in the states of Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram, and in all Union Territories except Delhi.

questions.question: Which Section of the Representation of People’s Act (RPA), 1951 deprives prisoners of their right to vote?
questions.solution: Section 62(5) of the RPA, 1951 states that no person shall vote at any election if he is confined in a prison, whether under a sentence of imprisonment or transportation or otherwise, or is in the lawful custody of the police.

questions.question: The Regulating Act of 1773 paved the way for the establishment of the Supreme Court at which location?
questions.solution: The Regulating Act of 1773 provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William, Calcutta (1774), comprising one Chief Justice and three other judges.

questions.question: Which south-eastern Dravidian language has been recommended by Odisha (in 2023) to be included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.solution: In July 2023, the Odisha cabinet approved a proposal to include the Kui language (spoken by the Kandha tribe) in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India.

questions.question: Which Section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) deals with the definition of 'rape'?
questions.solution: Under the old IPC, it was Section 375. In the new Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Section 63 defines 'rape' and Section 64 prescribes the punishment for it.

questions.question: Which of the following was widely considered as the ‘heaven born service’ for Indians during British rule?
questions.option_1: Military service on the Burma front
questions.option_2: The Indian Civil Service or ICS
questions.solution: The Indian Civil Service (ICS) was often referred to as the 'Heaven-Born Service' because of its immense power, prestige, and the fact that its members were recruited through a highly competitive exam in London.

questions.question: Which of the following is the proposed successor to the Information Technology Act, 2000?
questions.solution: The Digital India Bill (or Digital India Act) is the proposed legislation intended to replace the outdated IT Act, 2000 to address modern challenges like AI, cybercrime, and data privacy.

questions.question: Which Act prevents disrespect to the National Flag and National Anthem?
questions.option_1: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
questions.solution: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 prohibits the desecration of or insult to the country's national symbols, including the National Flag, the Constitution, and the National Anthem.

questions.question: Justice Indu Malhotra penned a famous dissenting opinion in which landmark judgement?
questions.solution: In the Sabarimala case (2018), Justice Indu Malhotra was the lone dissenter, arguing that 'notions of rationality cannot be invoked in matters of religion' and that judicial review should not interfere with essential religious practices unless they are harmful.

questions.question: Offences for which the police can arrest a person without an order from the court are called _________.
questions.solution: Cognizable offences are those for which a police officer may arrest without a warrant and start an investigation without court permission (e.g., murder, rape). Non-Cognizable offences require a warrant for arrest and court permission to investigate (e.g., defamation, cheating).

questions.question: Which act has been amended by the Supreme Court of India to provide equal rights to daughters in their ancestral property?
questions.solution: The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 amended the 1956 Act to give daughters the same rights as sons in ancestral (coparcenary) property. The Supreme Court further clarified in the Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) case that this right is retrospective.

questions.question: In which year was the Dowry Prohibition Act passed in India?
questions.solution: The Dowry Prohibition Act was enacted on May 20, 1961, to prohibit the giving or taking of dowry. It was one of the first major social reform legislations in independent India regarding marriage customs.

questions.question: In which year was the Arms Act passed in India?
questions.solution: The Indian Arms Act was passed in 1959 to regulate and restrict the acquisition, possession, manufacture, and sale of arms and ammunition in India, replacing the colonial-era Arms Act of 1878.

questions.question: In which year was the Special Marriage Act passed in India?
questions.solution: The Special Marriage Act was enacted in 1954. It provides a special form of marriage for the people of India and all Indian nationals in foreign countries, irrespective of the religion or faith followed by either party.

questions.question: According to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the process of insolvency resolution for companies should be completed in how many days?
questions.solution: Under the IBC, 2016, the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) must ideally be completed within 180 days. This can be extended once by up to 90 days, but the mandatory total timeline (including litigation) is 330 days.
